answers.reasoning: 48% of the number is 120, so 1% is 120 / 48 = 2.5 and the number is 250. Then 170% of 250 is 2.5 x 170 = 425.
One round is the perimeter: 2 x (700 + 500) = 2400 m. Four rounds need 4 x 2400 = 9600 m of wire.
Six numbers with average 15 add up to 6 x 15 = 90. The known numbers give 15 + 12 + 17 + 22 = 66, and (x+5) + (x-1) = 2x + 4. So 66 + 2x + 4 = 90, 2x = 20 and x = 10.
Three diameters make 6 equal sectors around the centre. The full turn is \(360^\circ\), so each sector's angle is \(360^\circ \div 6 = 60^\circ\).
Divide and multiply first: \(16 \div 4 = 4\) and \(2 \times 3 = 6\). Then 32 + 4 - 6 = 30.
Chairs cost 50 x 1065 = 53,250 rupees and blackboards cost 30 x 1645 = 49,350 rupees. The bill is 53,250 + 49,350 = 1,02,600 rupees.

Write everything in fifteenths: \(3 = \frac{45}{15}\), \(\frac{4}{5} = \frac{12}{15}\), \(2\frac{2}{5} = \frac{36}{15}\). Then \(\frac{45}{15} - \frac{12}{15} - \frac{7}{15} = \frac{26}{15}\), so the missing number is \(\frac{36}{15} - \frac{26}{15} = \frac{10}{15} = \frac{2}{3}\).

Half of a right angle is \(45^\circ\). One third of a right angle is \(30^\circ\), and \(15^\circ\) more is \(45^\circ\). The third angle is \(180^\circ - 45^\circ - 45^\circ = 90^\circ\). Two equal angles make two equal sides, so it is an isosceles right angled triangle.
The longest tape is the HCF of 1050, 750 and 425. 1050 = 2 x 3 x 5 x 5 x 7, 750 = 2 x 3 x 5 x 5 x 5 and 425 = 5 x 5 x 17. The only common factor is 5 x 5 = 25, so the tape is 25 cm.

(A) is false: 12 is divisible by 4 but not by 8. (B) is true because 3 and 5 have no common factor, so the number is divisible by 15. (C) is false: 8 is divisible by 2 and 8 but not by 16. (D) is true: for example 1 + 3 = 4, 5 + 7 = 12, 9 + 11 = 20, always a multiple of 4.
Melting keeps the volume the same. The cube's volume is 6 x 6 x 6 = 216 cubic cm. So 9 x 8 x height = 216, and height = 216 / 72 = 3 cm.
5 digit numbers run from 10,000 to 99,999. Their count is 99,999 - 10,000 + 1 = 90,000.
LXXIX = 50 + 10 + 10 + 9 = 79 and XXXIX = 39. Then 79 - 39 = 40, which is XL in Roman numerals.
180 minutes is 3 hours. At 65 km every hour the car goes 65 x 3 = 195 km.
446 = 400 + 40 + 6. 400 is CD (500 - 100), 40 is XL (50 - 10) and 6 is VI, giving CDXLVI.
In 5 hours she reads \(\frac{5}{7}\), so in 1 hour she reads \(\frac{1}{7}\). In 2 hours she reads \(\frac{2}{7}\).

A square's diagonals are equal and cut each other at right angles, so Statement-I is true. A rhombus's diagonals are perpendicular but usually of different lengths (they are equal only when the rhombus is a square), so Statement-II is false.
\(\frac{a}{b} = \frac{5}{15} = \frac{1}{3}\), so \(\frac{a}{b} + 1 = \frac{4}{3}\). Multiply by \(\frac{b}{a} = 3\) to get 4. Then b - a = 10, and 4 + 10 = 14.
In grams she bought 5640 + 3037 + 6008 = 14,685 g. She returned 2045 g, so she took home 14,685 - 2045 = 12,640 g = 12.640 kg.
One envelope costs 87.50 / 35 = 2.50 rupees. For 730 rupees we get 730 / 2.50 = 292 envelopes.
The LCM of 25, 40 and 60 is 600, which each divides exactly. Adding the remainder 9 gives 609, and 609 leaves 9 when divided by 25, 40 or 60.

A line segment with both end points on the circle is a chord, not a secant (a secant is a line cutting the circle at two points), so Statement-I is false. A chord need not pass through the centre; the chord through the centre is the diameter, so Statement-II is false too.
Compare per kilogram. Coffee at 24 rupees per 100 g costs 24 x 10 = 240 rupees per kg. Tea costs 180 rupees per kg. 240 : 180 = 4 : 3.
In minutes: Anil \(\frac{2}{3}\) h = 40, Ram \(\frac{3}{4}\) h = 45, Chetan \(\frac{1}{5}\) h = 12, Dharm \(\frac{5}{6}\) h = 50. Dharm exercised the longest.
The square's area is 30 x 30 = 900 square cm. The rectangle has the same area, so its length is 900 / 25 = 36 cm.
Cost price = 15,600 + 14,400 = 30,000 rupees. Selling price 31,200 gives a gain of 1,200. Gain % = \(\frac{1200}{30000} \times 100 = 4\%\).
630 bulbs make 630 / 15 = 42 groups of 15. Each group has 2 defective bulbs, so 42 x 2 = 84 are defective.

In the figure, y is vertically opposite the \(75^\circ\) angle, so \(y = 75^\circ\). The angles \(75^\circ\), \(42^\circ\) and x sit on one straight line, so \(x = 180^\circ - 75^\circ - 42^\circ = 63^\circ\). Then \(x + y = 63^\circ + 75^\circ = 138^\circ\).
Numbers below 60 ending in 3 are 3, 13, 23, 33, 43, 53. All are prime except 33 (= 3 x 11). The sum is 3 + 13 + 23 + 43 + 53 = 135.

answers.runnerUp: D, if lines in space are allowed: two lines can be skew (neither meeting nor parallel), which makes Statement-II false as well
answers.reasoning: A line goes on endlessly in both directions, so it has no end points; Statement-I is false (that describes a line segment). Two lines drawn on a flat surface either meet at a point or never meet (parallel), so Statement-II is true.
Boys' total = 5 x 12 = 60 and girls' total = 7 x 18 = 126. The group's total is 186 marks for 12 students, so the average is 186 / 12 = 15.5.

answers.value: A, B and C all pay Rs 420
answers.reasoning: Simple interest = principal x rate x time / 100. A: 3500 x 4 x 3 / 100 = 420. B: 4200 x 5 x 2 / 100 = 420. C: 2800 x 5 x 3 / 100 = 420. All three pay 420 rupees.
Each cube has volume 4 x 4 x 4 = 64 cubic cm. Three cubes joined together make 3 x 64 = 192 cubic cm (the cuboid is 12 cm by 4 cm by 4 cm).
41 has only the factors 1 and 41, so it is prime. That is exactly what makes a number prime, so the Reason is true and correctly explains the Assertion.
In 40 minutes (\(\frac{2}{3}\) hour) at 120 km/h the train covers 80 km. At 150 km/h it takes \(\frac{80}{150}\) hour = 32 minutes. It saves 40 - 32 = 8 minutes.
Convert \(50^\circ\)F to Celsius: \((50 - 32) \times \frac{5}{9} = 18 \times \frac{5}{9} = 10^\circ\)C. The difference is \(25^\circ\)C - \(10^\circ\)C = \(15^\circ\)C.

One-fifth of a right angle is \(18^\circ\), and two times that is \(36^\circ\). Its complement is \(90^\circ - 36^\circ = 54^\circ\). The supplement of \(54^\circ\) is \(180^\circ - 54^\circ = 126^\circ\).
Principal = interest x 100 / (rate x time). Anita: 850 x 100 / (5 x 4) = 4250 rupees. Sunita: 840 x 100 / (4 x 6) = 3500 rupees. The difference is 4250 - 3500 = 750 rupees.
The star in the figure has 12 sides, each 3 cm long. Its perimeter is 12 x 3 = 36 cm.

(A) Two acute angles add to less than \(180^\circ\), so they are not supplementary: not true. (B) Two obtuse angles add to more than \(180^\circ\): not true. (C) Twice half a right angle is \(90^\circ\), and \(90^\circ + 90^\circ = 180^\circ\): true. (D) An acute plus an obtuse angle is more than \(90^\circ\), so never complementary: not true.

Try * = 4: 3958 - 474 = 3484, which matches the pattern 3*8* with * = 4. Checking the others: with 6, 3958 - 676 = 3282 (not 3686); with 5, 3958 - 575 = 3383 (not 3585); with 3, 3958 - 373 = 3585 (not 3383).
The price went up by 72 - 15 = 57 rupees. As a percentage of the old price: \(\frac{57}{15} \times 100 = 380\%\).
At a 20% loss the selling price is 80% of the cost price. So cost price = 5840 x 100 / 80 = 7300 rupees.

Half a right angle is \(45^\circ\), and 5 times that is \(225^\circ\). A complete angle is \(360^\circ\), so the difference is \(360^\circ - 225^\circ = 135^\circ\), which lies between \(90^\circ\) and \(180^\circ\): an obtuse angle.
15 m 8 cm = 1508 cm. Divided into 4 equal parts: 1508 / 4 = 377 cm = 3.77 m.
Each letter of ABCD moves 10 places forward to give KLMN (A to K, B to L, C to M, D to N). Moving each letter of GHIJ 10 places forward gives QRST.

answers.runnerUp: D (33), if a different rule linked 24 and 11; no other simple rule fits an option
answers.reasoning: Half of 24 is 12, and one less is 11. In the same way, half of 64 is 32, and one less is 31.

Following the pattern 4 + 2 = 6, 40 + 20 = 60, we get 400 + 200 = 600, so the smiling face is 200. Two sad faces plus 2000 make 6000, so the two sad faces make 4000 and one sad face is 2000. The sum is 2000 + 200 + 2 = 2202.
Each number is paired with the number at the opposite end of its line, which is its square: 9 and 81, 6 and 36, 2 and 4. The fourth line joins 11 and ?, so ? = 11 x 11 = 121.
Filling the blanks with b, b, a, b gives a b a b a b a b a b a b: the pair "ab" repeated six times. The other choices break the pattern.

answers.reasoning: In Figures (1), (2) and (4) the matching symbols sit in opposite corners, crossing diagonally (in Figure (2) the two stars are diagonal). The letters are at positions 5, 10, 15, ?, 25 of the alphabet, going up by 5 each time. The missing position is 20, which is T.

answers.runnerUp: C, if the grouping is by plant part: ginger is an underground stem while carrot and beetroot are roots
answers.reasoning: Carrot, ginger and beetroot are the parts of the plant that grow under the ground. Tomato grows above the ground on the plant, so it is the odd one out.
36 = 6 x 6, 64 = 8 x 8 and 100 = 10 x 10 are perfect squares. 146 is not the square of any whole number (12 x 12 = 144), so it is the odd one out.
The figure shows 4 stars in Pattern 1, 8 in Pattern 2 and 12 in Pattern 3. Each pattern adds 4 stars, so Pattern n has 4 x n stars, and Pattern 9 has 4 x 9 = 36.
In each group the second letter is 3 after the first, and the third letter is 1 before the second (A, D, C). The first letters go A, E, I, so the next is M. Then M, P, O.
LEARN and LEAVE share LEA, and R comes before V. LESSON comes next (S after A). Then the LI words: LITTER before LIZARD since T comes before Z. The order is (B), (D), (E), (C), (A).
The Moon is a satellite. In the same way, the Earth is a planet.
Add the alphabet positions of the letters: BAT = 2 + 1 + 20 = 23. So DOG = 4 + 15 + 7 = 26.
The differences grow by 5: 5, 10, 15, then 20 and 25. So 35 + 20 = 55, and 55 + 25 = 80 checks.

answers.runnerUp: B, if the arm lengths are ignored; Figure (2) has the same corner and directions but with the long arm vertical
answers.reasoning: The bent arrow turns \(90^\circ\) clockwise each step, and the fifth figure is the same as the first. Its corner moves top right, bottom right, bottom left, so the fourth figure has its corner at the top left with a long arm pointing right and a short arm pointing down. Figure (4) shows this; Figure (2) has the long arm going down instead.
Each number in the middle row is 5 times the number above it: 3 x 5 = 15 and 7 x 5 = 35. The bottom row is 9 times the top row (27, 72, 63). So ? = 8 x 5 = 40.
On a sunny, hot day Arjun would wear a cap. In this code a cap is called a pencil, so the answer is Pencil.
Each letter is 2 places before the previous one: Z, X, V, T, R. Going back 2 more gives P, and 2 more gives N.
Multiply the two top numbers and divide by 3: 7 x 6 = 42 and 42 / 3 = 14; 9 x 2 = 18 and 18 / 3 = 6. So 6 x 4 = 24 and 24 / 3 = 8.
From biggest to smallest: the whale is the biggest animal, then the elephant, the lion, the cat, and finally the tiny honey-bee. That is (D), (C), (E), (A), (B).
The letters R, I, P, L, A make the word APRIL, which is the name of a month.

The mirror AB stands on the right, so left and right swap while top and bottom stay. The circle moves from the top left to the top right of the rectangle, the small square moves to the top of the left part, and the X moves to the bottom of the right part. Figure (3) shows exactly this.
In RTVX, MOQS and GIKM each letter is 2 places after the one before. In BDGJ the gaps are 2, 3, 3, so it is the odd one out.
If the day before yesterday was Wednesday, yesterday was Thursday and today is Friday. Tomorrow is Saturday, so the day after tomorrow is Sunday.
Madhubani painting is a traditional folk art from the Mithila region of Bihar, named after the Madhubani district.

answers.value: No rain, and crops may fail
answers.reasoning: A drought is a long period without rain, so there is too little water and crops may fail. Landslides, floods and tsunamis are the other options.
Abu Dhabi is the capital of the United Arab Emirates. Dubai is its biggest city, but not the capital.
The Valley of Flowers National Park is in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand.
Neil Armstrong was the first person to step on the Moon, on 20 July 1969, during the Apollo 11 mission.
Dissolving plenty of salt makes the water denser, so it pushes up harder on the egg and the egg floats. This is the usual salt-water experiment.
Gandhiji led the Dandi March (Salt March) from Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad, to Dandi in March to April 1930, to break the British salt law.

answers.reasoning: SAARC stands for South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, a group of South Asian countries including India.

answers.reasoning: The stomach churns and mixes food with digestive juices, so Statement I is true. Doctors have also found that digestion slows down when a person is sad, angry or worried, so Statement II is true as well.

Bachendri Pal became the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest, in 1984.

answers.value: Because it has the saltiest water
answers.reasoning: The Dead Sea is one of the saltiest water bodies in the world. Very salty water is dense and pushes a person up, so she floats even if she cannot swim.
The roots take in water and nutrients from the soil and send them up the stem to the rest of the plant.
The tabla is a pair of Indian drums. The tanpura and sitar are string instruments and the harmonium is a keyboard instrument.
Rabindranath Tagore wrote Gitanjali, and won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1913.

answers.reasoning: The Kalbeliyas are a community of Rajasthan known as snake charmers, who traditionally travel with snakes and make them dance to the been.
The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in Agra in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
A thermometer measures temperature. A barometer measures air pressure, a microscope shows tiny things and a telescope shows faraway things.
Jupiter is the largest planet in our Solar System, much bigger than Saturn, Uranus or Earth.
The lungs take in air when we breathe in and let it out when we breathe out.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India, from 1950 to 1962.
